value: This article provides a comprehensive overview of knot theory and its generalization, link theory, both fundamental branches of topology. It defines knots as one-dimensional embeddings of circles in three-dimensional space and links as multi-component extensions, exploring their properties through concepts like isotopy, knot complements, and Reidemeister moves. A significant portion details various knot and link invariants crucial for classification, such as crossing numbers, polynomial invariants (Jones, HOMFLY, Alexander), and homology theories (Khovanov homology). The text illustrates these ideas with specific examples like the trefoil, Hopf, and Borromean links, while also providing a foundational context by outlining core principles, spaces, and theorems from general topology.
